items.mainDefect: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response, but callers expect their normal refresh shape with `.data`, so they break.

secondary.defect: The sync fetch call has no content-type header, no timeout and no response.ok check.

items.mainDefect: The Salesforce connection getter refreshes the token on every connection with no expiry check, which adds a network call each time.

secondary.defect: The `.success` check on the parseRefreshTokenResponse result is redundant because that function throws on failure.
The Salesforce refresh skips the refreshOAuthTokens wrapper, so it ignores credential sync and never uses the sync endpoint.

items.mainDefect: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time.

secondary.defect: An array-valued secret header goes through the comparison without being checked.
zod parse, JSON.parse and symmetricDecrypt have no try/catch, so invalid input gives a 500 instead of a 4xx.
The decrypted keys are never checked to be an object.

items.mainDefect: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which leaks timing information.

secondary.defect: Array-valued headers are not handled and a missing header is not explicitly rejected.

items.mainDefect: Google CalendarService saves the zod safeParse wrapper {success, data} as the credential key instead of the parsed data.

secondary.defect: In credential-sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined.

items.mainDefect: zoho-bigin passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint gets the wrong calcomUserId.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, the helper returns a fetch Response but the code reads tokenInfo.data (an axios shape), so it breaks.

items.mainDefect: Google CalendarService saves the zod SafeParseReturnType {success, data} as the credential key.

secondary.defect: In credential-sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws.

items.mainDefect: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` in the parseRefreshTokenResponse schema become fixed bogus keys, so the schema always fails in sync mode.

secondary.defect: `refresh_token` is set to the literal string 'refresh_token' when missing, and that placeholder gets saved.

items.mainDefect: Google CalendarService saves the zod SafeParse result {success, data} as the credential key, so the top-level tokens are lost.

secondary.defect: parseRefreshTokenResponse is given the already-merged googleCredentials instead of the refresh response, so it validates the wrong object.

items.mainDefect: The computed keys in the parseRefreshTokenResponse schema become a fixed junk key, so the schema always fails in sync mode and the helper throws.

secondary.defect: The literal 'refresh_token' placeholder is injected when the refresh token is missing, which overwrites real refresh tokens for callers that spread `data` into the stored credential (Office365, Zoom).

items.mainDefect: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects the user id, so sync mode fetches credentials for the wrong user.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, the fetch Response has no `.data`, so axios-style callers (zoho-bigin, Zoho CRM, HubSpot) throw on `tokenInfo.data.error`.

items.mainDefect: Google CalendarService saves the zod SafeParse result {success, data} as the credential key, which corrupts the stored credential.

secondary.defect: In credential-sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws.

items.mainDefect: zoho-bigin passes credentialId instead of the cal.com userId to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong user's credentials.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, the helper returns a fetch Response with no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data.error` throws.
